summary: The dominant cause of INC-012 is storage exhaustion at the shared ledger-db datastore: the /var/lib/postgresql/data volume filled monotonically (94.73% at 14:00Z -> 98% at 14:48:20Z -> pinned 100.0 from the 14:56Z bucket) driven by WAL being retained rather than recycled by the inactive 'analytics_cdc' replication slot, which was already announcing tens of GB of retained WAL from 13:02:25Z. PostgreSQL then began PANICing on WAL writes ('could not write to file pg_wal/xlogtemp... No space left on device') from 15:01:01Z, and every write path that reaches ledger-db fails with the identical ENOSPC signature — payment-service's 354 'ledger write failed' ERROR lines (first 15:00:26Z) and order-service's independent 'INSERT INTO orders failed' lines, which no payment-service code fault can explain. payment-service v6.0.0 (dep-6203, 14:46:00Z) is the only change in the window but is not the ongoing cause: it was rolled back at 15:12:00Z, after which the error rate did not step down and the disk stayed pinned at 100% with PANICs continuing. Confidence in this root cause is medium (0.70): the fault and the fix target (reclaim the volume and restore WAL recycling) are well verified, but the origin of the slot inactivity is unobservable in this telemetry.

ranked_hypotheses.title: ledger-db volume exhausted by uncontrolled WAL retention; storage ENOSPC is the dominant ongoing cause (deploy neither necessary nor sufficient)
ranked_hypotheses.statement: The ledger-db datastore exhausted its /var/lib/postgresql/data volume. Disk climbed steadily and monotonically (94.73% at 14:00Z -> 97.85% at 14:35Z -> 98% at 14:45-14:48Z -> pinned 100.0 from the 14:56Z bucket to end of window), and PostgreSQL began PANICing ('could not extend file' / 'could not write to file pg_wal/xlogtemp: No space left on device') from 15:01:01Z through 16:57:21Z. Because the storage layer cannot allocate, every write that grows a relation fails with ENOSPC: payment-service's ledger writes (354 identical ERROR lines) and order-service's independent 'INSERT INTO orders' writes both fail. The fill is driven by WAL that is being retained rather than recycled; the ledger-db log repeatedly reports 'replication slot ... is inactive; retaining <n> MB of WAL' (5 WARN lines from 13:02:25Z through 14:49:47Z, with retained-MB values oscillating in the tens of GB the whole time), so a slot with no managed/known consumer is the identified retention source. The precise instant retention began and the consumer-side cause are NOT observable in this telemetry (no slot-state or WAL-bytes metric exists; the 'analytics_cdc' consumer has no catalog entry). payment-service v6.0.0 (dep-6203, 14:46Z) is the only change of any kind across all services in the window; it is not the ongoing cause (rollback at 15:12Z changed nothing), but it is not positively exonerated as a transient write/WAL-generation contributor to an already-climbing fill. Fix target: reclaim the ledger-db volume and restore WAL recycling / drop the orphaned slot — not payment-service code.

causal_chain.claim: A ledger-db replication slot ('analytics_cdc') is inactive and its WAL is being retained instead of recycled; the condition is long-running, visible from 13:02:25Z, with retained WAL oscillating in the tens of GB and no drop/activation/retention-cap log ever appearing
No managed or catalogued consumer owns the slot: 'analytics-cdc' is not_found for both logs and metrics and appears in no known_services entry — so the WAL consumer is an unmanaged orphan
Retained WAL grows rapidly through the 14:34-14:50Z window: 33916 MB (14:34:05Z) -> 69518 MB (14:46:32Z) -> 77371 MB (14:49:47Z)
The volume fills: 94.73% (14:00Z) -> 97.85% (14:35Z) -> 98% (14:48:20Z) -> 100.0% pinned from the 14:56Z bucket onward
PostgreSQL can no longer extend storage: PANIC 'could not extend file: No space left on device' from 15:01:01Z, continuing to 16:57:21Z

payment-service's write path surfaces the identical storage error: 354 ERROR 'ledger write failed: ... No space left on device', first 15:00:26Z, with error_rate stepping from ~0.2% to ~60% at the 14:54-14:58Z bucket
order-service fails on the identical storage error ('INSERT INTO orders failed: No space left on device'), proving a shared datastore fault rather than a payment-service code fault

Failure is fast and load-independent: p99 flat (~293-348 ms), request_rate flat (~100 req/s), CPU flat (~30%), slow_queries flat — consistent with blocked-on-storage ENOSPC, not query cost or a one-code-path fault
The fault persists after the v6.0.0 rollback: error_rate unchanged 55-70% through 16:55Z; disk pinned at 100% with PANICs continuing — no storage fix occurred

assumptions: The retained WAL volume (tens of GB, reported continuously since 13:02:25Z) is the dominant contributor to the fill on a volume that was already 94.7% full at 14:00Z; no WAL-bytes or WAL-generation-rate series exists, so 'retention vs generation rate' cannot be separated quantitatively.

The slot-inactive condition is the retention source rather than a coincidental log line; replication_lag_ms shows only a slow pre-existing trend (~3.1-3.5s before 14:34Z, no step) so it does not confirm the retention onset instant, and the consumer-side cause of the inactivity is not queryable (no analytics/CDC component in the catalog).

Errors are not split by ledger entry type or route anywhere in telemetry (F19, F21, F23); the single observed signature is storage ENOSPC, but a complete non-truncated enumeration of all 354 lines was not obtained.
The ~30% mean / 60% peak error fraction is broad storage-path failure of writes reaching ledger-db; no per-endpoint or per-entry-type split is recoverable.

ranked_hypotheses.title: Unverifiable datastore-level config/retention change at ledger-db (no audit surface exists)
ranked_hypotheses.statement: A datastore-level configuration change at ledger-db (e.g. max_wal_size / wal_keep_size / archive_command / replication-slot retention or cleanup policy) could in principle have reduced WAL recycling headroom and driven the volume to 100%. The critique is correct that this cannot be positively excluded: get_config_changes returns count=0 for both the reported and the wider window, but its coverage is unlabeled, and there is NO separate ledger-db parameter/tuning audit surface — get_config_changes and get_deployments are the only datastore-level surfaces and both return count=0. Historical search for a slot-retention/WAL-parameter-change cause finds nothing (HIST-114 is an operational inactive-slot fill, category resource_exhaustion, not a config edit). So this remains a live category-level alternative with a distinct fix target (config revert) that is unverifiable rather than negative.

causal_chain.claim: An unrecorded config/retention change lands at ledger-db, e.g. disabling slot cleanup or shrinking WAL-retention headroom
WAL accumulates and the volume fills (94.7% at 14:00Z -> 100% by 14:56Z), producing ENOSPC writes failures that cascade to payment-service and order-service
No such change is visible: get_config_changes for ledger-db and all-services returns count=0 in both windows, and no ledger-db tuning/deployment record exists
No queryable audit surface exists for datastore parameter/retention history — the probe verdict is UNVERIFIABLE rather than negative

assumptions: Such an unrecorded change exists despite every queried window returning count=0.

It could be timed to the WAL-growth window even though the slot-inactive retention explicitly predates the whole incident window (WARNs from 13:02:25Z), which makes a 14:34-15:00Z config trigger less parsimonious than the already-logged inactive slot.

ranked_hypotheses.title: payment-service v6.0.0 mandate flow writes an unsupported ledger entry type (contract fault)
ranked_hypotheses.statement: The new MANDATE_HOLD entry type introduced by payment-service v6.0.0 is not accepted by the ledger writer, so mandate-flow writes fail and lift the payment error rate to 60%. Under this reading the observed 'could not extend file' errors would be a separate concurrent storage issue.

causal_chain.claim: dep-6203 deploys payment-service v6.0.0 at 14:46:00Z, adding mandate endpoints and ledger entry type MANDATE_HOLD
Mandate endpoints write MANDATE_HOLD entries to the ledger
The ledger rejects the new entry type, failing those writes and lifting the payment error rate to ~60% by 14:56Z

assumptions: A ledger-side validator would reject MANDATE_HOLD.
The 354 identical storage errors are not the dominant failure path.
The direct endpoint-level A/B (mandate routes vs legacy routes failing at equal rate) could not be obtained and cannot be — the fields do not exist in telemetry.
ranked_hypotheses.rejection_reason: Every observed error is a storage-capacity signature ('could not extend file: No space left on device') with no validator/constraint/payload exception anywhere in sampled logs (F8, F18, F22); the same error independently kills order-service's orders path (F10); the ledger volume was already ~98% at 14:48:20Z and climbing, with retained WAL reported from 13:02:25Z, well before the 14:46Z deploy (F9, F24, F26, F37); a contract fault would not produce a datastore-wide ENOSPC, would not persist unchanged after the 15:12Z rollback with storage still pinned at 100% and PANICs continuing (F27, F28); flat p99/request rate and flat slow-query count give no latency or load signature of a failing code path (F14, F15, F17). No telemetry distinguishes a MANDATE_HOLD failure at all — 'MANDATE_HOLD', 'entry_type' and 'mandate' match 0 log lines across payment-service, api side and ledger-db (F20, F21), so the mechanism is unsupported by the only available attribution fields. Rejection is inferential (no direct A/B route split was obtainable) but the mechanism is contradicted on multiple independent axes.

ranked_hypotheses.title: External bank-partner-api degradation driving payment failures
ranked_hypotheses.statement: bank-partner-api degraded and caused the payment failures, with the ledger write errors a downstream consequence. HIST-105 is a precedent for exactly this mode.

causal_chain.claim: bank-partner-api degrades or returns 5xx
payment-service payment attempts fail against the partner
Failure/rollback load spills into ledger writes that then fail on storage

ranked_hypotheses.rejection_reason: Purely speculative: bank-partner-api has has_telemetry=false (F6), so nothing verifies it, whereas the ledger-db storage failure is fully verified with a matching error signature (F8, F9). A partner failure would not produce ENOSPC at ledger-db, would not spill into order-service's independent order-insert failures (F10), and would not coincide with a monotonic disk climb pinned at 100% (F16). Request rate is flat with no retry storm (F15).

ranked_hypotheses.title: Deploy ordering: v6.0.0 shipped before a required companion ledger migration/config
ranked_hypotheses.statement: payment-service v6.0.0 began serving mandate traffic before a companion migration or config landed, so a subset of ledger writes fail.

causal_chain.claim: dep-6203 deploys v6.0.0 at 14:46:00Z
Companion ledger-side migration/config for MANDATE_HOLD is absent
A subset of ledger writes fails, lifting the error rate

assumptions: A missing migration would manifest as ENOSPC rather than a validation/constraint error.
ranked_hypotheses.rejection_reason: No migration tooling and no migration entries appeared in deployment or config output, so no companion change is evidenced at all (gap). The observed mechanism is filesystem exhaustion at ledger-db killing order-service too (F9, F10), which the ordering of a payment-service release cannot explain. Timestamps contradict ordering outright: the volume was already 98% full at 14:48:20Z with retained WAL reported from 13:02:25Z, before the 14:46Z deploy (F9, F24, F26, F37).

facts.statement: ledger-db is the failing storage layer: it logged disk usage 98% on /var/lib/postgresql/data at 14:48:20Z and then PostgreSQL PANIC 'could not extend file: No space left on device' from 15:01:01Z, with retained WAL from an inactive replication slot at 33916 MB (14:34:05Z) -> 69518 MB (14:46:32Z) -> 77371 MB (14:49:47Z).

ledger-db disk_used_pct climbed monotonically from avg 94.88 (14:00Z) to avg 99.98 / max 100.0 at 14:56:00Z, then stayed pinned at 100.0 for every bucket through 16:56:00Z — exactly as the payment error rate jumped.

payment-service emitted 354 ERROR logs, all one signature: 'ledger write failed: ERROR: could not extend file: No space left on device', first seen 2026-06-01T15:00:26Z through 16:57:54Z; the returned sample is truncated (40 of 354) but no payload/contract error appears among the entries.

order-service is affected by the same storage fault: 236 ERROR logs all of signature 'INSERT INTO orders failed: No space left on device', first at 15:00:42Z — the blast radius extends beyond payment-service, which a payment-service code fault cannot explain.

The inactive 'analytics_cdc' slot condition is long-running and pre-existing: the WARN 'retaining <n> MB of WAL' pattern runs continuously from 13:02:25Z through 14:49:47Z, at least 1h32m before the 14:46Z release, with retained WAL oscillating in the tens of GB.

PostgreSQL PANICs on WAL writes: 153 ERROR lines of 'PANIC: could not write to file pg_wal/xlogtemp.<n>: No space left on device' span 15:01:01Z to 16:57:21Z, i.e. the retained-WAL volume, not the ledger entry path.

ROLLBACK TEST (payment-service): error_rate did NOT recover after the 15:12:00Z rollback — avg 61.18 at 15:05Z and 60.36 at 15:10Z pre-rollback, then 63.21 at 15:15Z, 64.07 at 15:20Z, and ~60-64% through 16:55Z, with no step down.

ROLLBACK TEST (storage): ledger-db disk_used_pct was already pinned at 100 after the 15:12Z rollback and PANICs continued to the end of the window; no storage fix occurred and the fault did not clear.

payment-service error_rate was flat ~0.2-0.3% through the 14:54Z bucket, then stepped to avg 30.41 / max 60.8 at the 14:58Z bucket (avg 30.17 / max 60.8 at 14:56Z) and stayed ~60-63% thereafter — a step change, not gradual degradation.

The only deployment across ALL services in both 14:30Z-15:10Z and 13:00Z-15:30Z was payment-service v6.0.0 (dep-6203, 14:46:00Z), adding 'mandate create/approve endpoints' and a 'new ledger entry type MANDATE_HOLD', rolled back at 15:12:00Z; no config or feature-flag changes were recorded in either window (count=0).

No telemetry attributes the failures to a mandate/entry-type path: 'MANDATE_HOLD' matches 0 payment-service log lines, 'entry_type' matches 0 in both payment-service and ledger-db, 'mandate' matches 0 in payment-service, and ERROR lines carry no entry_type, route/endpoint or mandate field.

Load, latency and query-cost families are excluded: payment-service p99 latency is flat (min 292.28, max 348.32, mean 320.95 ms), request_rate is flat (~100 req/s, min 89.92, max 110.09), CPU stays ~29-33%, and ledger-db slow_queries_per_min is unchanged (min 0.41, max 1.75, mean 1.0).

No consumer service owns the 'analytics_cdc' replication slot in the catalog: query_logs and query_metrics for 'analytics-cdc' returned not_found, and the enumerated known_services list contains no analytics/CDC/consumer component.

No log records the slot being dropped, activated, deactivated, or a retention cap being hit: a full-range ledger-db query for 'analytics_cdc' returned only the same 5 WARN 'inactive; retaining <n> MB of WAL' lines, and 'retention' returned total_matched 0.

The only datastore-level audit surfaces available (get_config_changes and get_deployments) both return count=0 for ledger-db in 14:00Z-15:10Z, and no separate ledger-db parameter/tuning audit surface exists — a datastore-level config change is UNVERIFIABLE rather than negative.

Historical precedent matches a WAL/disk cause, not an entry-type cause: HIST-114 (2025-04-18) was ledger-db disk full from retained WAL with resolution 'Dropped slot', and no past incident attributes ledger write failures to a max_wal_size/wal_keep_size/archive_command edit.
bank-partner-api (external, vendor-owned) has has_telemetry=false, so its health cannot be confirmed from telemetry and must be treated as unverifiable.

assumptions: The retained WAL volume (tens of GB, reported continuously since 13:02:25Z) is the dominant contributor to the fill on a volume already 94.7% full at 14:00Z; no WAL-bytes or WAL-generation-rate series exists, so 'retention vs generation rate' cannot be separated quantitatively.

The slot-inactive condition is the retention source rather than a coincidental log line; replication_lag_ms shows only a slow pre-existing trend (~3.1-3.5s before 14:34Z, no step), so it does not confirm the retention onset instant, and the consumer-side cause of the inactivity is not queryable.
Errors are not split by ledger entry type or route anywhere in telemetry; the single observed signature is storage ENOSPC, but a complete non-truncated enumeration of all 354 lines was not obtained.
The ~30% mean / 60% peak error fraction is broad storage-path failure of writes reaching ledger-db; no per-endpoint or per-entry-type split is recoverable.
payment-service v6.0.0 is not positively exonerated as a transient write/WAL-generation accelerant into an already-filling volume, even though the rollback test shows it is not the ongoing cause.

(demoted from facts: no verified observation backs it) Timing ordering: ledger-db disk exhaustion signals (98% at 14:48:20Z, PANIC 15:01:01Z) and the payment error-rate onset (~14:54-14:58Z) both precede/coincide with the first payment 'ledger write failed' log at 15:00:26Z — the storage fault begins before the payment-service write-error stream.

timeline.event: ledger-db begins continuously logging WARN 'replication slot analytics_cdc is inactive; retaining <n> MB of WAL' (33247 MB), establishing a long-running pre-existing retention condition well before the incident.
ledger-db disk_used_pct already 94.73-94.88%; replication_lag_ms already elevated 3.1-3.5s with no step change — a slow pre-existing trend.
ledger-db logs the first in-window inactive-slot WARN with retained WAL 33916 MB; the slot is retaining WAL, shrinking disk headroom.

payment-service v6.0.0 (dep-6203) deployed — the only deployment across all services in the 13:00Z-15:30Z window; adds mandate create/approve endpoints and the MANDATE_HOLD entry type. Retained WAL measured at 69518 MB at 14:46:32Z.
ledger-db reports disk usage 98% on /var/lib/postgresql/data, i.e. the volume is nearly full before the payment error onset; retained WAL 77371 MB at 14:49:47Z.
payment-service error_rate steps from ~0.2% to avg 30.17 / max 60.8; ledger-db disk_used_pct reaches and pins at 100.0 (max) for this bucket onward.
First payment-service ERROR 'ledger write failed: ERROR: could not extend file: No space left on device' (party of 354 such lines through 16:57:54Z).
order-service begins emitting 'INSERT INTO orders failed: No space left on device' (236 lines) — independent blast radius on the same shared storage layer.
PostgreSQL at ledger-db begins PANICing on WAL writes: 'could not write to file pg_wal/xlogtemp.<n>: No space left on device' (153 lines through 16:57:21Z).
Incident INC-012 [SEV-1] reported by on-call SRE: payment-service error rate ~60%, ledger write failures.
payment-service v6.0.0 rolled back; ledger-db disk already pinned at max 100 and PANICs continue.
Post-rollback: payment-service error_rate does NOT recover (63.21 at 15:15Z, 64.07 at 15:20Z, ~60-64% through 16:55Z), and storage stays pinned at 100%.
End of window: PANICs and ENOSPC write failures are still ongoing; no storage fix has occurred.

recommended_actions.action: Immediately reclaim space on the ledger-db /var/lib/postgresql/data volume to break the ENOSPC deadlock (e.g. expand the volume / clear non-PostgreSQL files) and restore PostgreSQL's ability to write WAL, so that PANICs ('could not write to file pg_wal/xlogtemp...') stop and writes can resume.
recommended_actions.rationale: The datastore is pinned at 100.0% with PostgreSQL PANICing on WAL writes from 15:01:01Z to 16:57:21Z; every write reaching ledger-db (payment-service and order-service) fails until space is freed.

recommended_actions.action: Inspect and drop/deactivate the orphaned 'analytics_cdc' replication slot (after confirming no active consumer needs it), then verify WAL recycling resumes and disk_used_pct falls well below 100%.
recommended_actions.rationale: The inactive slot's WAL retention is the identified retention source; the hardened action targets the cause, not payment-service, and mirrors the HIST-114 precedent resolution 'Dropped slot'.

recommended_actions.action: Do NOT re-apply payment-service v6.0.0 as a fix; keep the 15:12:00Z rollback in place until storage health is restored and monitored.
recommended_actions.rationale: The rollback test shows no recovery after 15:12Z with storage still pinned at 100% and error_rate unchanged, so v6.0.0 is not the ongoing cause and redeploying it would not help.

recommended_actions.action: After space is reclaimed, confirm recovery by verifying: ledger-db disk_used_pct drops and holds below 100%, PostgreSQL PANIC lines cease, payment-service error_rate returns toward ~0.2-0.3%, and order-service 'INSERT INTO orders' ENOSPC errors stop.
recommended_actions.rationale: These are the exact signals that both confirmed onset and survived the failed rollback; they give a clean, testable recovery criterion tied to the verified mechanism.

recommended_actions.action: Add a replication-slot / WAL-retention alert (retained-WAL bytes and slot-active state) plus an alert on disk_used_pct, since none currently exists — the slot condition was only visible via three WARN log lines and disk was already 94.7% before the incident.
recommended_actions.rationale: The retention was announced as early as 13:02:25Z yet ran unchecked into a 100% fill; the HIST-114 precedent resolution also added a slot-lag alert. Existing metrics expose no slot state or WAL-bytes series.

recommended_actions.action: Register/inventory the 'analytics_cdc' WAL consumer (owner, liveness, restart policy) so that a stopped consumer no longer silently pins WAL; today no analytics/CDC component exists in the catalog.
recommended_actions.rationale: The origin hop of the incident (why the slot's consumer stopped) is unobservable because no consumer service exists in the service catalog and no slot-active/WAL-bytes metric is exposed.

recommended_actions.action: Set and enforce a controlled WAL-retention cap / slot-inactivity cleanup policy (bounded wal_keep_size / max_slot_wal_keep_size plus automated inactive-slot handling) so a stalled consumer cannot fill the volume unbounded in future.
recommended_actions.rationale: Retained WAL oscillated in the tens of GB over 1h47m; a bounded retention policy prevents a single stalled consumer from exhausting the volume again while preserving replication capability.

recommended_actions.action: Add entry_type / route / mandate identifiers and endpoint attribution to payment-service ledger-write error logs so a future 'new entry type' contract question can be answered directly instead of inferred.
recommended_actions.rationale: The contract-fault hypothesis could only be rejected inferentially because 'MANDATE_HOLD', 'entry_type' and 'mandate' match 0 log lines and no route field exists, so today's telemetry cannot split failures by entry type or route.

recommended_actions.action: Expose a datastore parameter/retention change-audit surface for ledger-db (e.g. log max_wal_size / wal_keep_size / archive_command / slot-retention edits) so a datastore-level config change can be confirmed or excluded.
recommended_actions.rationale: get_config_changes and get_deployments both return count=0 for ledger-db and no independent parameter surface exists, leaving that alternative categorically unverifiable rather than refuted.

data_gaps: Origin of the slot inactivity: no analytics/CDC consumer exists in the telemetry catalog, and no slot-state or WAL-bytes metric exists, so what stopped the WAL consumer at ~14:34Z (or earlier) cannot be determined. This bounds the conclusion to 'ledger-db-side WAL/slot retention' without naming the consumer-side trigger.

No replication-slot metric: the slot active/inactive state is observable only via three WARN log lines, and there is no WAL-bytes or WAL-generation-rate series, so retention vs generation rate cannot be separated quantitatively and the precise retention onset is not pinned.

Datastore config audit absent: get_config_changes and get_deployments both return count=0 for ledger-db with no independent parameter/tuning surface, so an unrecorded max_wal_size / wal_keep_size / archive_command / slot-retention change cannot be confirmed or excluded.

Entry-type / route attribution is physically absent from telemetry: 'MANDATE_HOLD', 'entry_type' and 'mandate' match 0 log lines and ERROR lines carry no route or mandate id, so the per-entry-type and per-endpoint failure split cannot be produced.
payment-service memory_pct and db_pool_in_use were not obtained (budget exhausted), so memory/connection saturation is unverified (CPU verified healthy only).

Full quantitative blast radius is not established: error-rate/latency metrics for order-service, ledger-db, settlement-service and others were not obtained; blast radius for order-service rests on log evidence only.
The returned payment-service ERROR sample is truncated (40 of 354), so a complete per-message audit of all failures was not possible.
ledger-db exposes no write-latency metric (write_latency_p99_ms returned not_found), so p99 write latency to the datastore cannot be measured directly.
bank-partner-api has has_telemetry=false, so it could not be checked as an alternative upstream.
what_would_change_the_conclusion: Evidence that ledger-db disk_used_pct was NOT near capacity before the payment error onset (e.g. a correct disk series showing free space throughout 14:45Z-16:00Z) would break the storage-exhaustion mechanism.

Identification of validator / constraint / payload / HTTP 4xx errors on ledger writes, or log/missed telemetry showing MANDATE_HOLD writes failing while legacy entry types succeed, would restore the contract-fault hypothesis (H2).
Any observed recovery of payment-service error_rate coinciding with the 15:12:00Z rollback (a step down at or after 15:12Z) would implicate v6.0.0 rather than storage.

Evidence that error-rate elevated without any ENOSPC signature — e.g. failures confined to mandate routes while legacy routes stay healthy and storage remains below capacity — would move the ranking away from H1.

A documented, timestamped datastore-level config/retention change at ledger-db (max_wal_size / wal_keep_size / archive_command / slot-retention) in 14:00Z-15:10Z would make H4 a live competitor and shift the fix target to a config revert.

Confirmation that the 'analytics_cdc' slot was active and WAL recycling healthy throughout, with disk fill attributable instead to an unrelated large object or non-WAL data, would redirect the root cause away from WAL retention.
Telemetry showing a bank-partner-api degradation at ~14:55Z correlated with payment failures would revive H3 (currently unverifiable and contradicted by shared ENOSPC plus order-service collateral).

findings.statement: Across ALL services, the only deployment in 14:30Z–15:10Z (and in the wider 13:00Z–15:30Z window) was payment-service v6.0.0, dep-6203, deployed 14:46:00Z, adding 'mandate create/approve endpoints' and a 'new ledger entry type MANDATE_HOLD'; status rolled_back at 15:12:00Z.
No config or feature-flag changes were recorded for any service in either the reported window (14:30Z–15:10Z) or the wider 13:00Z–15:30Z window: count returned 0 both times.

payment-service's dependency edges are: -> ledger-db (kind 'db'), -> bank-partner-api (kind 'external'), -> kafka (kind 'queue-produce'), and inbound api-gateway -> payment-service (kind 'http'). ledger-db and kafka are both flagged shared=true (owner platform), meaning other services can affect payment-service through these shared components.

The v6.0.0 deployment at 14:46:00Z precedes the reported ~14:55Z symptom onset by about 9 minutes; no other change in the 14:30Z–15:10Z window has a timestamp closer to 14:55Z (config=0, other deployments=0).

Historical precedent for ledger write failures does NOT match a 'new ledger entry type' cause: HIST-114 (2025-04-18) was ledger-db disk full from retained WAL ('no space left on device', 'write failures', resolution 'Dropped slot'), and HIST-111 (2025-05-22) was an index-less report query causing sequential scans/high db cpu. Also HIST-105 (2025-11-19) shows a prior payment-service failure caused by external bank partner API 5xx.

findings.statement: payment-service's own CPU is not saturated and shows no change across the incident: cpu_pct stays ~29-33% (min 26.56, mean 30.11) in every bucket from 14:30 to 16:57, including throughout the 60% error period — consistent with healthy-but-blocked on external storage rather than resource exhaustion.

Timing ordering: ledger-db disk exhaustion signals (98% at 14:48:20Z, PANIC 15:01:01Z) and payment error-rate onset (~14:54-14:58Z) both precede/coincide with the first payment 'ledger write failed' log at 15:00:26Z; the storage fault at ledger-db begins before the payment-service write-error stream.

payment-service error_rate was flat ~0.2% (avg 0.21-0.24, max <=0.32) through every bucket from 14:00:00Z to 14:48:00Z, then jumped to avg 30.17 / max 60.8 in the 14:56:00Z bucket and remained elevated ~60-63% (avg 60.35-63.62) through 16:56:00Z. This is a step change, not a gradual degradation.

payment-service p99 latency is FLAT across the incident: 14:00Z-16:56Z buckets all sit in a tight band (min 292.28, max 348.32, mean 320.95 ms) with no elevation after the 14:56Z error-rate onset (e.g. 323.02 at 14:56Z, 324.42 at 15:12Z, 315.61 at 16:56Z). The failure mode is fast failure, not latency growth.

payment-service request_rate is also flat at ~100 req/s throughout (min 89.92, max 110.09, mean 100.11), including during the 60% error period (avg 101.59 at 14:56Z, 103.14 at 15:12Z, 100.10 at 16:56Z). Traffic did not collapse or spike, so the 30%+ error fraction is not a load-driven effect.

ledger-db disk_used_pct climbed monotonically from avg 94.88 (14:00Z) to avg 99.98 / max 100.0 at 14:56:00Z, then stayed pinned at 100.0 for every bucket through 16:56:00Z. The datastore's disk filled to capacity exactly as the payment error rate jumped at 14:56Z.

ledger-db slow_queries_per_min is unchanged across the incident (min 0.41, max 1.75, mean 1.0; 14:48Z avg 0.97 vs 15:04Z avg 0.97 vs 16:56Z avg 0.67). The ledger datastore is NOT suffering slow/complex queries — the write path fails on storage capacity, not query cost.

payment-service's error log stream is a single storage signature, not a payload/contract error: 354 of 378 matched log entries in 14:46Z-16:59Z are ERROR 'ledger write failed: ERROR: could not extend file: No space left on device' (first 15:00:26Z), with only 4 WARN and 20 INFO otherwise. No mandate/entry-type-specific exception or HTTP 4xx validation error appears in the returned sample.

findings.statement: A bounded filter for the entry type 'MANDATE_HOLD' across payment-service logs in 14:46Z-16:59Z returned total_matched=0 (not truncated, partial=false), i.e. the string MANDATE_HOLD appears in no payment-service log line in or after the release window.

The literal token 'entry_type' returns 0 matches in BOTH payment-service (tc-032) and ledger-db (tc-038) logs over 14:46Z-16:59Z, and the string 'mandate' returns 0 matches in payment-service logs (tc-033). The ledger-db logs also contain no 'entries' ERROR lines (tc-040). The entry-type attribution the task needs is simply not emitted anywhere in the returned telemetry.

The single failure signature is a storage-capacity error ('could not extend file: No space left on device') emitted by payment-service, whose blast radius is not confined to new entry types: the same 'No space left on device' family is what stops writes. Combined with the established fixed error rate of ~30% mean (60% peak) and unchanging request_rate, the write path fails at the storage layer for whatever writes reach ledger-db, regardless of entry type — there is no evidence of a MANDATE_HOLD-specific code path failing.

findings.statement: Only three 'inactive slot' WARN lines exist in the whole 14:25Z-16:59Z ledger-db log range (14:34:05Z, 14:46:32Z, 14:49:47Z; total_matched 3, truncated false), i.e. the slot-inactive condition was reported in the 14:34-14:50Z window and not re-emitted after 14:49:47Z, consistent with the consumer stop/detection occurring well before the payment error onset.

The only configuration/flag-change surface reachable via the tools is get_config_changes; scoped to ledger-db for 14:00Z-15:10Z it returns count=0, changes=[], partial=false. No separate ledger-db parameter-change log, tuning/infra record, or datastore config history is exposed as a distinct surface — the same call is the only one available, and its coverage is unlabeled.

No ledger-db deployment/tuning release record exists in 14:00Z-15:10Z either: scoped deployment query for ledger-db returns count=0, and the all-services query in the same window returns exactly one deployment, payment-service dep-6203 (v6.0.0, 14:46:00Z), which lists only application code changes ('mandate create/approve endpoints','new ledger entry type MANDATE_HOLD') — no max_wal_size, wal_keep_size, archive_command or slot-retention parameter item.

The only datastore-tuning signal in the incident record is the ledger-db dependency node (owner platform, has_telemetry=true) and its shared=true flag; the graph metadata exposes no parameter/retention history field, only node type/owner/shared/telemetry. So even the datastore's own node record carries no config-audit surface.

Historical search specifically for a slot-retention/WAL-parameter CHANGE cause returns only HIST-114 ('ledger-db disk full from retained WAL', category resource_exhaustion, root_cause 'Inactive replication slot retained WAL until disk filled'), whose resolution was 'Dropped slot; added slot-lag alert' — an operational/fill event, not a config/parameter change. No past incident in the index attributes ledger write failures to a max_wal_size/wal_keep_size/archive_command edit.

findings.statement: Bounded existence verdict on the probe: no independent ledger-db config/retention audit surface exists in the tool set. Both available datastore-level surfaces (get_config_changes and get_deployments) return count=0 for ledger-db in 14:00Z-15:10Z, so a datastore-level config change (max_wal_size, wal_keep_size, replication-slot retention, archive_command, slot cleanup timing) is UNVERIFIABLE rather than negative.

No consumer service owns the 'analytics_cdc' replication slot in the catalog: both query_logs and query_metrics for service 'analytics-cdc' returned not_found, and the enumerated known_services list contains no analytics/CDC/consumer component (only api-gateway, auth-service, order-service, portfolio-service, pricing-engine, market-data-service, payment-service, settlement-service, notification-service, exchange-gateway, ledger-db, user-db, redis-cache, kafka, exchange-api, bank-partner-api, kyc-provider, email-provider).

No log anywhere records the slot being dropped, activated, deactivated or a retention cap (max_wal_size/wal_keep_size/slot cleanup) being hit: a full-range ledger-db query for the literal token 'analytics_cdc' returned only the same 5 WARN 'replication slot ... is inactive; retaining <n> MB of WAL' lines (total_matched 5, truncated false); a query for 'retention' in ledger-db returned total_matched 0; and kafka and settlement-service contained 0 'slot' lines.

The slot-inactive condition is NOT a 14:34Z onset but a long-running pre-existing state: the WARN 'retaining <n> MB of WAL' pattern runs continuously from 13:02:25Z (33247 MB) through 13:12:19Z (77137 MB), 13:37:25Z (37927 MB), 13:48:09Z (92599 MB), 13:52:50Z (82259 MB), 14:16:25Z (78423 MB)... to 14:49:47Z (77371 MB), i.e. at least 1h32m before the release, with retained WAL oscillating in the tens of GB the whole time.
